title: Fats Waller's happiness and what Autrey learned from him
summary: Fats was always happy on and off stage, preached enjoying life, and taught musicians by showing them at the piano.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Was Fats a happy person? Do you know?
Very, very, very, at all times. Very. Immensely.
This was not just a front then.
Naw, heck no. No.
Because I've heard so much of the idea that underneath it all he was rather disappointed that his music -- he wasn't playing Bach, and --

Nah, nah, he was happy. I mean -- and he would preach that. That was his -- be happy. Do what makes you happy. I mean that was his check on own life. He would tell people, you know. "Use it." (Raspberry) don't do it. Forget it. Do what you want to do. Make yourself happy." You know. He said life is short. Life is short. Be happy." You know?

That was -- he -- looked like he was -- to me, he was in a rush, keeping things moving, going forward, just move forward, be happy, enjoy life. Be gay, enjoy this, and be nice, to and this person, and enjoy, and you know. To me that's the way he impressed me.
Musically, Herman, what did you get from Fats?

Oh, many things. Many things. Much. Because I mean a lot of times you'd be playing things, you might say -- he'd say well, how about this? How about that? Uh, stop and think, or he would play it on piano. Listen to this. And you'd have to, and you'd think of what he meant, or what he was saying, and you'd go from there. You know?
Don't be -- in other words, you don't pay any more -- he didn't want to see -- he didn't want -- he never was a grouch.
He didn't want you to be a grouch. Be a nice guy. Be lovable. Love people. Love life. Love things. You know?
He -- that's -- that's the way he impressed the world, as far as I'm concerned.
Well certainly that's the way he impressed the world. This was what you saw of Fats on stage, but I was wondering, off stage --
No.
-- he was the same person?
The same --
He didn't have --
No.
He must have had low moments, didn't he? When he felt unhappy?
Well --
Or did you never see them?

I never saw them, because if he did I didn't know what they were about. You know. I -- it would have had to have been his secret, or it was personal, maybe, or maybe, I don't know anythings that happened to him, like that. I don't know.
Did -- in the years that you knew Fats, did he change at all? Or was he always the same?
Always the same.
No difference.
No. No. No.
